title: Savings Helix: adaptive bundling initiative for dynamic batching, KV-prefetch, and quant profiles
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Savings Helix is an initiative to validate and productize a combined 'bundle' approach that automatically selects per-request serving tactics (batch size, KV prefix prefetching, and quantization profile) to minimize unit cost while meeting customer-defined quality and latency SLOs. Hypothesis: a small set of tested bundles, selected dynamically by request profile and customer policy, can deliver >=15% median token cost savings on production traffic with <=2% quality regression and no more than a 10% increase in p99 latency. This ticket tracks the roadmap, success metrics, experiments, and rollout plan for the initiative.
success_metrics: Reduce median per_token_service_cost by >=15% on targeted workloads (chat + short completion archetypes)
Maintain mean model-quality delta <= 2% on LM-eval-probe prompt set (auto-eval)
p95 latency change <= +20ms; p99 latency change <= +60ms
Increase cache hit rate for KV prefix caching from baseline by >=12% on repetitive sessions
milestones: 2025-09-15: Design doc and bundle matrix approved by Eng + Research
2025-09-30: Runtime knobs implemented (dynamic batch selector + KV prefetch API) and unit tests merged
2025-10-07: Quant profile library (q8/q4/ptq variants) validated on small model and integrated into canary harness
2025-10-15: Canary experiment (10% traffic) live with automatic rollback hooks
2025-11-01: Metrics evaluation; prepare rollout PRD and rollback thresholds
2025-11-15: Gradual roll to 50% for eligible customers or full rollout depending on signal
recent_updates: 2025-09-10: Eng spike showed dynamic batch selector reduces GPU kernel launches by ~8% for short sequences; tradeoff: tail latency increase for some multi-turn sessions noted
2025-09-22: Research validated q4_k_m profiles on two open models; avg perplexity delta within 1.3% for conversational prompts; memory footprint reduced by ~2.4x
2025-09-28: Console team added per-route knob for 'bundle preference' and a toggle for 'quality-first' vs 'cost-first' policies; awaiting UX copy review
2025-10-02: Canary harness wired to monitoring dashboard and synthetic eval triggers; initial 24h run shows cost savings ~12% on canary cohort, quality signal within guardrail
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end pipeline exists to define bundles and associate them to route/customer policies via Console
Automated selection policy can be simulated offline and audited before canary
Canary experiment must show cost saving >=12% with LM-eval-probe quality delta <=2% for 72h window before expanding
Fallback semantics documented and implemented: on quality or latency regression beyond thresholds, system reverts to baseline model/flags automatically
Observability: per-request explanation recorded (why a bundle was chosen) and surfaced in Console logs for 30 days
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Quantization introduces subtle semantic regressions for long-context summarization. Mitigation: Run targeted eval subset and add 'quality-first' policy to bypass quant profiles for long-context routes.
Risk: KV prefetch memory pressure for high-concurrency customers. Mitigation: per-tenant cache soft-limits and LRU eviction, circuit-breaker for cache growth spikes.
Risk: Batching increases p99 latency for low-parallelism customers. Mitigation: dynamic batch timeout heuristics and per-route max_batch_size override.
Risk: Incorrect bundle selection may cause billing visibility confusion. Mitigation: Console shows per-token cost breakdown and a bundle label; billing reports include bundle tags.
stakeholders: Legal & Compliance: Daniel Kwon (for enterprise rollout considerations)
notes_for_engineering: Start with a small orthogonal set of bundles: {small-batch+prefetch+q8}, {med-batch+no-prefetch+q4_k_m}, {latency-first: small-batch+no-quant}
Add capability to label each request with 'bundle_reason' (heuristic+score) to aid offline analysis
Expose lightweight sim harness to test new bundle rules against historical traces before canary
Document memory and GPU kernel trade-offs for each quant profile to inform autoscaler configs
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): run on synthetic traffic and internal tenants for 2 weeks
Phase 1 (canary): enable for 10% of eligible production traffic with strict auto-rollback; monitor cost/quality/latency windows
Phase 2 (staged): expand to 25% then 50% with manual checkpoints and CS-managed pilot customers
Phase 3 (general): enabled by default with per-route opt-out and Console visibility
consumer_notes: Target workloads: chat sessions under 4 turns, short completions under 128 tokens, high-repetition prompt templates benefit most
Not targeted initially: long-context summarization flows and RLHF fine-tune evaluation endpoints
qa_plan: Unit tests for bundle selector logic and KV-prefetch API
Integration tests against runtime-1.21 images with quant profiles enabled
Synthetic regression suite using LM-eval-probe + user-submitted golden prompts
Chaos tests for cache eviction and rollback pathways
regulatory_considerations: Ensure no customer data leaves VPC when prefetching in private deployments; prefetch respects per-tenant data residency rules
Add audit events for bundle selection decisions for enterprise compliance review
long_term_notes: If successful, Savings Helix will be converted into an extensible marketplace of pre-validated bundles and a policy engine that lets customers define custom cost/quality trade-offs per route. Next-phase work will explore model-split routing (cheap left-to-right draft followed by expensive refine) and per-tenant learned bundle selection models.
communication_plan: Weekly sync with Eng + Research on Thursdays 10:00am PT
Fortnightly stakeholder readout with CS and Sales; prepare a one-pager for customer pilots
Pre-rollout announcement in #product and #sre channels with runbook and rollback steps
open_questions: What is the canonical auto-eval metric and threshold for conversational quality that correlates with CS NPS?
Should bundle selection be per-request or per-session by default?
How to present cost attribution in billing reports without overwhelming customers?
